_README: Benchmark for the F14-B ferroelectric polarization change Delta P (polarization.py, T2-3). The core TB computes the KSV ELECTRONIC Zak-phase polarization difference between a [001]-polar (P4mm) displacement and the centrosymmetric reference. We compare its SIGN/REVERSAL and ORDER OF MAGNITUDE to DFT ferroelectric polarizations of halide perovskites.

dft_references.source: P. Bhumla, D. Gill, S. Sheoran, S. Bhattacharya, arXiv:2108.03683 (2021) (verified web 2026-05-24)
dft_references.note: large rhombohedral distortion -> upper end of the FE-perovskite range
DFT/measured FE polarizations of distorted halide perovskites are typically a few uC/cm^2 (up to tens for strong distortions).

tb_results._method: polarization.ferroelectric_polarization_difference: KSV electronic Zak phase, [001] B-cation displacement (make_polar_kashikar13_builders), CsPbI3, n_kxy=4, n_kz=24. Delta P = (e/2 pi A)(phi(d)-phi(0)).
tb_results.note: Electronic contribution only (ionic separate). Grows ~linearly with displacement; reverses sign with the polar direction (odd in d to leading order).

comparison.sign_reversal: RIGOROUS (the defining FE property): Delta P(-d) = -Delta P(+d) to leading order (4.7% asymmetry at d=0.05, growing with d^2). Gauge-invariant.
comparison.magnitude: TB electronic Delta P ~ 1-8 uC/cm^2 (d=0.05-0.40 A) is the SAME ORDER as DFT FE perovskite polarizations (a few uC/cm^2). Category C->B for sign+order.
comparison.honest_note: This is the ELECTRONIC Berry-phase contribution only; the DFT values are the TOTAL (ionic + electronic). The order-of-magnitude match is encouraging but quantitative agreement is not claimed (ionic term separate; SK-TB/Blount on absolutes). The rigorous, gauge-invariant content is the sign reversal and that Delta P vanishes for the centrosymmetric reference.
